Why it helps: Actual gross vs the employee's fixed entitlement. Zero pay (0) and wrong-decimal pay (~10x) sit far from the normal 0.3-3 range.
Share of gross taken in deductions. Excess tax pushes it above 1; a missing deduction lowers it. NaN when gross_pay is 0.
Take-home share of gross. Negative or tiny values signal over-deduction. NaN when gross_pay is 0.
Checks the data-dictionary identity 'gross = earned fixed + overtime + variable'. Should be ~1.0; a shifted decimal breaks it. NaN when the expected gross is 0.

Formula: monthly_fixed_gross / median monthly_fixed_gross for the same role_id in the previous calendar month
Why it helps: Pay relative to the prior month's role norm. A salary far above its role is a role/grade mismatch. NaN when no prior-month role reference exists.
Month-on-month change in the fixed salary. A drop suggests payment on a stale (pre-revision) salary; a large jump suggests a wrong grade. NaN for an employee's first month.
Overtime hours are capped at 50 by policy; very large values indicate an overtime spike.
Overtime as a share of gross. Normal is near 0; a spike dominates the payslip. NaN when gross_pay is 0.

Formula: pf_employee / the employee's previous-month pf_employee (only when the previous PF > 0)
Why it helps: PF is stable month to month; a drop to 0 means provident fund was not deducted. NaN when there is no previous month or previous PF was 0 (PF-exempt employees).
